newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian police foil backpacker killer jailbreak bid.
newsitem.headline: Australian police foil backpacker killer jailbreak bid.

text.p: Australian police on Saturday foiled an elaborate attempt by Australia's most notorious serial killer to escape from jail.

Ivan Milat, drug baron George Savvas and two others had planned to escape from Maitland jail in the state of New South Wales, but police were prepared for the attempt because of an undercover intelligence operation conducted over several weeks.
"We have been gathering information about the escape plans and we were one step ahead of the prisoners at all times," Corrective Services assistant commissioner Rod Woodham said in a statement.
"The prisoners will be transferred and segregated and our joint investigations of the people involved in the escape plan are continuing."
A Corrective Services spokeswoman declined to release details of the escape plan as it involved several people from outside the jail. They were still being questioned, she said.

"My understanding is that they (the prisoners) were going to go over a wall at some stage, but it was quite an elaborate plot and it involved outside people smuggling things into them," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
Milat, 51, is serving a life sentence for the murder of seven backpackers, including five Europeans, outside Sydney.
Savvas, 47, is serving a 30-year sentence for conspiring to import heroin.
He escaped from another jail in July last year and was recaptured on March 20 at an exclusive inner city Sydney restaurant after police were tipped off.
